draft.title: The Agricultural Revolution
card: From the 1700s, British farmers tried new ways to grow more. Crop rotation, such as the four-field system with turnips and clover, kept soil fertile. Selective breeding produced bigger animals.
Common land was shared by villagers for grazing animals and growing food. Under enclosure, it was fenced off and became the private property of landowners, often by Acts of Parliament.
Larger enclosed farms using the new methods produced more food. They needed fewer workers to do it.
Many villagers lost their use of common land and their farm work. Many moved to towns to look for jobs, which meant more people were available to work in the new industries.
draft.remember: New methods and enclosure made more food with fewer workers, and many people moved to towns.

a.q: What did enclosure change in the British countryside?
opts: Shared common land became private property
Farm land was handed to the villagers who worked it
Landowners were stopped from fencing their fields
Farmers returned to older and simpler crop methods
a.why: Enclosure meant common land was fenced off and owned by landowners. It did not give land to villagers, which is the reverse of what happened, because villagers lost their use of it.
a.clue: Think about who could use the land before and after fences went up.

b.q: In the 1790s, Tom's family in an English village grazed their cow on the common. After enclosure, the common was fenced off. Why did Tom's family most likely move to a town?
opts: They lost the common and farm work, so they sought jobs
The new methods made food so scarce that they starved
Landowners ordered all villagers to leave the country
The common land was turned into factories in the village
b.why: Enclosure took away the common land, and larger farms needed fewer workers. This pushed many families to look for work in towns. The new methods produced more food, not less, so food shortage is not the reason.
b.clue: Consider what Tom's family lost, and how many workers the bigger farms needed.

a.best: Shared common land became private property

b.best: They lost the common and farm work, so they sought jobs
